text:
gabi (SRE): Quick announce: were running a controlled network-path failover drill Thu 2026-09-09 01:30-02:00 UTC. Goal: validate cross-AZ routing policies, ensure KV cache rewarm, and measure SLO burn for a deliberate 10m asymmetric routing period. This is a drill, not a real incident.

rory (EngRuntime): Drill scope: flip route preference from primary -> secondary in eu-west-1 for 10m, then revert. Will only affect control-plane traffic and control-plane-proxied hosted-api routing (data plane unaffected).

mo (Oncall): Please confirm rollback automation: abort if 5xx rate >15% OR p95 latency increase >200ms sustained for 3m. Who has the abort key?

gabi (SRE): Abort key is with mo (oncall) + rory. tanya, we'll publish the burn-rate tolerance.

tanya (SLO): For the drill window we'll set a temporary maintenance marker and increase acceptable burn-rate to 4x for 10m. Will not trigger SLA credits. I'll update the SLO dashboard and annotate the event id: DRILL-2026-09-09-01.

sam (ProdOps): I'll post a short advisory on status.redwood.ai and email enterprise contacts with subject "Planned drill: network-path failover (control-plane)". Template: one-sentence impact + ETA to completion + mitigation (we recommend Dedicated customers pin model versions).

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: #ops-drill-1862346789 will be created 15m prior and subscribe #eng-sre, #prodops, #support.

rory (EngRuntime): Warmup plan: run lightweight synthetic generator to prefill KV and a short burst against each control-plane proxy after flip. Script (run from ops hosts):

```bash
models=(gpt-small-3 gpt-embed-1)
for m in "${models[@]}"; do
  for i in {1..20}; do
    curl -s -X POST https://api.internal/v1/warmup \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMUP_KEY" \
      -d '{"model":"'$m'","prompt":"drill warmup"}' &
  done
  wait
done
```

rory (EngRuntime): We'll also disable non-critical control-plane jobs for the 30m window and set autoscale offsets to avoid overloading fallback nodes.

mo (Oncall): I will watch datadog dash `drill-1862346789` and keep the abort play handy. mo -> will also keep exec-oncall notified.

gabi (SRE): Support prep: sam, can you produce canned replies? SRE will include the quick checklist: expected transient 503s, some 504s on tails, and rare 429s if throttles engage.

sam (ProdOps): Yup. Also adding a short FAQ: "Why are you doing this?" answer: "to verify routing fallbacks and reduce blast radius in real incidents".

tanya (SLO): After the drill we'll run a quality-sanity: sample 200 tokens across models to verify output regressions <1% for generation and embeddings cosine drift <0.005. We'll attach results to the postmortem.

rory (EngRuntime): Monitoring hooks: set alert if 5xx >10% for any 3m window (notify #eng-sre), and auto-abort if >15% for 3m. Also tracking p95 latency, error breakdown by 503/504/429.

ops-bot: Channel created: #ops-drill-1862346789. Pins: runbook, warmup script, rollback play, postmortem template.

gabi (SRE): Logistics: start warmup 20m before flip, flip at 01:30, hold 10m, revert at 01:40, then run post-validation for 10m. If all good, tidy and close channel with short note and link to postmortem.

mo (Oncall): Acks. Will keep watch and press abort if needed.

sam (ProdOps): Advisory drafted, sending in 10m.

tanya (SLO): I'll push SLO annotations and the DRILL- event to the observability timeline.

gabi (SRE): Thanks all. Keep messages concise during the window. We'll collect logs and attach to postmortem. If anyone sees anything surprising during the drill, shout in #ops-drill-1862346789 and tag mo/rory.
